items.title: The growth rocket takes aim at healthcare's time thieves
items.summary: In just under three years, Tandem Health has gone from an idea on an airplane to an extremely fast-growing, billion-valued health technology company with tens of thousands of doctors and healthcare workers across Europe using Tandem's AI assistant every day.
items.title_original: Tillväxtraket tar sikte på vårdens tidstjuvar
items.summary_original: På knappt tre år har Tandem Health gått från en idé på ett flygplan till ett extremt snabbväxande miljardvärderat hälsoteknikbolag med tiotusentals läkare och vårdanställda över hela Europa som varje dag använder Tandems AI-assistent.

items.title: Moscow's setback: "Putin's loss of prestige"
items.summary: The Russian forces from the Wagner Group and the Afrika Korps would save Mali's rule. Instead, they are pressured by the country's jihadists. It is a heavy loss of prestige for President Putin.
items.summary_original: De ryska styrkorna från Wagnergruppen och Afrikakåren skulle rädda Malis styre. I stället pressas de av landets jihadister. Det är en tung prestigeförlust för president Putin.

items.title: Substitute teacher convicted of 16 rapes against children
items.summary: A man in his 30s who was employed as an unauthorized teacher at a school in Gävle is sentenced to seven years in prison for 16 rapes against children, Gefle Dagblad reports. The man was charged at the end of February with 54 rapes against 27 different children and young people in Sweden, Denmark, Ireland and Norway. All younger than 15 years and the youngest being nine years old. According to the newspaper, the man allegedly found his victims on Snapchat and allegedly made them perform sexual acts on themselves in front of the camera.  Most of the crimes occurred while the man was employed at the school.
items.title_original: Lärarvikarie döms för 16 våldtäkter mot barn
items.summary_original: En man i 30-årsåldern som varit anställd som obehörig lärare på en skola i Gävle döms till sju års fängelse för 16 våldtäkter mot barn, rapporterar Gefle Dagblad. Mannen åtalades i slutet av februari för 54 våldtäkter mot 27 olika barn och unga i Sverige, Danmark, Irland och Norge. Samtliga yngre än 15 år och det yngsta vara nio år gammal. Enligt tidningen ska mannen ha hittat sina sina offer på Snapchat och ska ha fått dem att utföra sexuella handlingar på sig själva framför kameran.  De flesta brotten inträffade under tiden mannen var anställd på skolan.

items.title: Focus on Ukraine, NATO and Middle East as Maria Malmer Stenergard attends NB8 meeting in Estonia
items.summary: Minister for Foreign Affairs Maria Malmer Stenergard is attending a meeting of Nordic-Baltic foreign ministers (NB8) in Kuressaare, Estonia, on 29–30 April. The agenda includes support to Ukraine, constraining Russia’s aggression in the region, boosting European security, current NATO issues and developments in the Middle East.

items.title: Sweden announces more than SEK 2.7 billion in humanitarian assistance to the world’s most vulnerable
items.summary: The world’s humanitarian needs are immense. There are a record number of conflicts, with more than 300 million people in need of urgent humanitarian assistance. And there is a risk of needs further increasing this year. For this reason, Sweden is announcing more than SEK 2.7 billion in humanitarian assistance to the world’s most vulnerable for 2026.

items.title: Government presents new support package for global health
items.summary: The Government has presented a new support package for global health totalling SEK 72 million for 2026. The support includes SEK 50 million in core support to the International Vaccine Institute (IVI) for work with vaccines in low-income countries, and SEK 2 million to the Partnership for International Politics and Diplomacy for Health, a collaboration between Karolinska Institutet and the Stockholm School of Economics. The Government is also giving SEK 20 million in support for donations of medical technical equipment and medical supplies.

items.title: Sweden and France held a meeting in the Nuclear Steering Group in Paris
items.summary: In his speech on nuclear deterrence doctrine, given on March 2nd at Ile Longue, President of the French Republic Emmanuel Macron announced bilateral strategic dialogues with the European partners involved, to establish the concept of forward deterrence.

items.title: EU adopts 20th sanctions package against Russia
items.summary: The EU’s 20th package of sanctions includes comprehensive measures that hit the Russian economy, including Russia’s energy revenues and the shadow fleet. The package also includes measures against sanctions evasion, crypto services and access to sensitive technology used on the battlefield.

items.title: Christina Nilsson wins Government’s Music Export Prize
items.summary: Minister for International Development Cooperation and Foreign Trade Benjamin Dousa has presented the Government’s 2025 Music Export Prize to internationally acclaimed Swedish opera singer Christina Nilsson. The Government’s Special Prize was awarded to rock group The Hives, and the Government’s Honourable Mention went to production company MXM Music for the Taylor Swift Project.

items.title: The French and Swedish Ministers for Gender Equality reaffirm partnership to combat human trafficking for sexual exploitation in Europe and globally
items.summary: On 13 April, the French and Swedish Ministers for Gender Equality Aurore Bergé and Nina Larsson met in Paris. They discussed their national experiences in preventing and combating sexual exploitation and reaffirmed their commitment to the French - Swedish joint strategy to combat human trafficking for sexual exploitation in Europe and globally.

items.title: Government presents proposals to increase pressure on illegal settlements in West Bank
items.summary: The Government takes an extremely serious view of the continuing settlement policy and the increased settler violence in the West Bank, and is therefore proposing new measures in the form of an expanded differentiation policy. The Israeli Government’s actions in the West Bank violate international law.

items.title: Government announces SEK 15.4 million in support to democracy and cultural heritage preservation in Ukraine
items.summary: The Government is presenting a new support package focused on democracy and cultural heritage preservation in Ukraine of SEK 15.4 million for 2026–2028, SEK 8.7 million of which is for 2026. The support includes SEK 3 million to the National Democratic Institute (NDI), SEK 0.9 million to the Council of Europe and SEK 1.5 million to the OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights (ODIHR) for 2026. The support to cultural heritage initiatives includes SEK 10 million to Gotlands Museum for 2026–2028.

items.title: Sweden increases humanitarian support to Lebanon
items.summary: Sweden is announcing an additional humanitarian support package to Lebanon of SEK 70 million. The support is being provided in light of the country’s worsening humanitarian situation due to the conflict between Israel and Hezbollah. It will contribute to addressing basic needs, protecting the civilian population and creating security for those who have been hardest-hit by the conflict.

items.title: Government approves support to cultural heritage preservation in Ukraine
items.summary: The Government has decided on new support totalling SEK 12 million for initiatives preserving the cultural heritage of Ukraine through UNESCO for 2026–2027. The support will ensure the protection and long-term preservation of cultural heritage sites threatened by the war.

items.title: Joint Statement by President Macron and Prime Minister Starmer, Co-chairs of the International Summit on the Strait of Hormuz: 17 April 2026
items.summary: Today, France and the United Kingdom convened 51 countries for an international summit on the Strait of Hormuz. The meeting underlined the determination of the international community to support freedom of navigation, to stand up for international law, and to protect global economic stability and energy security.

items.title: Government proposes bills to strengthen efforts for accountability for Russia’s aggression against Ukraine
items.summary: Today, the Government is taking an important step to ensure accountability for Russia’s aggression against Ukraine. Through two Government Bills, it is proposed that Sweden join the Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine and accede to the Convention establishing an International Claims Commission for Ukraine. Sweden has played an active role in the establishment of both mechanisms.
